title: Energy in Food Comes from the Sun
seo_title: Grade 5 Energy in Food Worksheets: Energy from the Sun, Plants and Animals
standard_text: Use models to describe that energy in animals’ food (used for body repair, growth, motion, and to maintain body warmth) was once energy from the sun.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets on energy in food (NGSS 5-PS3-1): plants capture the sun's energy, animals use food for growth, repair, motion and warmth, and food chains that trace energy back to the sun. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: The energy in all food was once energy from the sun.
key_sub: Plants capture sunlight and store energy in food. Animals eat it and use the energy for body repair, growth, motion and keeping warm.
body_html:
How to think about it

The energy in all food first came from the sun.

  • Plants capture energy from sunlight and use it to make food (sugar) from carbon dioxide and water. This is called photosynthesis. The energy is stored in leaves, stems, roots, fruits and seeds.
  • Animals cannot make their own food. They get energy by eating plants, or by eating animals that ate plants.
  • Animals use that energy for body repair, growth, motion and keeping warm.
Example

A cheetah chases a gazelle that ate grass. Where did the cheetah's energy come from first?

cheetah ← gazelle ← grass

The grass captured sunlight.

Answer: the sun

Example

A puppy grows, runs, heals a scratch and stays warm. What gives it the energy for all of this?

It cannot make food from sunlight.

It eats food that stores energy.

Answer: the energy stored in its food

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get their energy from the soil. Soil gives a few nutrients; the energy comes from sunlight.
  • Thinking meat-eaters do not depend on the sun. Every food chain begins with a plant.
  • Thinking food only gives materials. It also gives energy for growth, repair, motion and warmth.
  • Drawing energy arrows backward. Energy moves from the sun to plants to animals.

faq.q: Where does the energy in food come from?
faq.a: From the sun. Plants capture sunlight and store its energy in the food they make. Animals get the energy by eating plants or animals that ate plants.

faq.q: What do animals use energy from food for?
faq.a: Body repair, growth, motion and keeping their bodies warm.

faq.q: Do meat-eating animals get energy from the sun?
faq.a: Yes, indirectly. The animals they eat got their energy from plants, and the plants got it from the sun.
The process plants use to capture light energy and make sugar from carbon dioxide and water. The sugar stores the energy.
